hero.title: BIOMEDICAL ENGINEERING IN FRANCE
hero.subtitle: Students interested in **studying biomedical engineering,** medical technology, health equipment, biotechnology and the application of engineering principles to medicine have opportunities in France.

overview: Students interested in **studying biomedical engineering,** medical technology, health equipment, biotechnology and the application of engineering principles to medicine have opportunities in France.
Students may study undergraduate science programs before moving on to biomedical engineering, or they may follow the engineering-school path beginning after high school.
Biomedicine is a mix of biology and engineering . For students from abroad , note that not all schools offer a specialized ** **3-year bachelor in biomedical engineering **.**
Some French schools offer **five-year engineering programs**; others require students to complete two or more years of university study before entering the engineering specialization.
****Edu Hawk worldwide** study abroad guidance** can help students to explore these opportunities and to understand the requirements involved in pursuing education overseas.

sections.title: 1. Can I pursue biomedical engineering in France after Class 12?

items: Yes but the routes are different. You can apply for an appropriate **bachelor's degree programme** or a longer **engineering route**. Certain specialized courses in biomedical engineering require prior university training.

sections.title: 2. How long does it take to study biomedical engineering in France?

items: A **Licence in biomedical sciences** usually takes three years. A full engineering-school pathway is typically five years after high school, depending on the program and the entry route.

sections.title: 3. Do I need French for biomedical engineering in France?

items: Many undergraduate courses are taught in French, and some require proof of **French language proficiency**. Before you apply, check the language of instruction and the tests they accept for each program.

sections.title: 4. How much does it cost to study biomedical engineering in France?

items: Biomedical engineering tuition fees in France vary by institution and qualification. The published public-university Licence reference for 2026–2027 is €178 a year for eligible French and EU students and €2,902 for non-EU students subject to differentiated fees. Fees for engineering-school and private-school can vary.

sections.title: 5. What will I do after I study biomedical engineering?

items: Career opportunities include medical device development, biomedical instrumentation, hospital equipment management, quality assurance, regulatory affairs, health technology, and research. Some specialist jobs require additional study or a qualification in engineering.

Check the exact qualification and its **recognition and accreditation status** before you enroll.
For French engineering qualifications verify that the *Diplôme d’ingénieur* is licensed and accredited by the **Commission des titres d’ingénieur (CTI)**.
A bachelor’s degree or Licence in biomedical sciences is a distinct qualification and should not be referred to as an accredited engineering diploma.
Students should check:
* The specific **degree** awarded.
*  Official status of recognition and accreditation of the program.
* Duration and **ECTS credits**.
* Access to laboratory work, internships and industry placements.
* Eligibility to undertake further study or to be granted professional recognition in the country where they intend to work.
Healthcare technology and medical-device development may also be governed by industry-specific standards and regulations.
**Biomedical engineering graduates** can find jobs in **medical-device companies, healthcare technology, diagnostics, research, medical equipment services and biotechnology**.
**Career opportunities in biomedical engineering include:**
* - **Biomedical engineering**.
*  **Design/development engineer, medical devices.
* **Clinical engineer or hospital equipment specialist
* - Engineer in biomedical instrumentation.
* - Associate, quality assurance or regulatory affairs
* **R\&D (research and development) assistant or engineer**.
*  **Medical imaging or health technology professional.
* Digital health professional, biomedical systems.
The position offered will be based on your qualification, practical experience, technical specialization, language skills and work authorization.
Master's-level or recognized engineering qualification is required for some engineering and research positions.
Bachelor's-level graduates may be accepted for some technical and support roles.
The biomedical engineering salary depends on the employer, location, experience and position.
